score.notes: A disciplined East-Asian pagoda temple read head-on, and the strongest dimension is its coherence as a whole. Proportion is deliberate: a dark ashlar base, a red colonnaded middle with evenly spaced bays, and a two-tiered green crown give a clear base→middle→crown with a believable upward taper — the tiered roofs with their upturned ridge accents and gold finial sit convincingly over the colonnade. The palette is genuinely harmonious and identity-giving: verdigris-green roofs as the dominant, lacquer-red columns as the support, and gold plus turquoise-diamond panels as accents — colorful without tipping into garish. Detail is purposeful — recessed bays behind the columns, gold stud courses, patterned frieze/soffit panels, a framed central doorway with a lit interior — and it rewards a look. Fidelity is clear and characterful: it unmistakably reads as a grand temple with real presence and an obvious entrance. What keeps each dimension at strong rather than exceptional: the wall fields between columns and above the entablature are fairly flat, the gold stud/diamond panels repeat mechanically rather than developing across the facade, the relief depth is shallow (mostly one-block in/out), and the crown tiers are close copies rather than a developed progression. All are easy-to-name improvements, so this tops out as a very good, not apex, build.
